items.label: Hero podnaslov
items.sr: Prilagođene tetovaže rađene ručno, napravljene da traju ceo život.
items.en: Custom tattoos made by hand, built to last a lifetime.

items.label: Galerija, uvodni tekst
items.sr: Bez filtera, bez ulepšavanja. Ovako izgleda kad zaraste.
items.en: No filters, no touch-ups. This is how it looks once healed.

items.label: Svako od nas radi svoje. Ne pokušavamo da …
items.sr: Svako od nas radi svoje. Ne pokušavamo da budemo sve za svakoga, zato svaki rad izgleda kao da je rađen baš za tebe.
items.en: Each of us does our own thing. We do not try to be everything to everyone, that is why every piece looks like it was made just for you.

items.label: Bez iznenađenja. Evo tačno šta te čeka od …
items.sr: Bez iznenađenja. Evo tačno šta te čeka od prve poruke do zarastanja.
items.en: No surprises. Here is exactly what to expect, from first message to healed.

items.label: Random Tattoo Studio je mali, umetnički st…
items.sr: Random Tattoo Studio je mali, umetnički studio u srcu Beograda. Verujemo da svaka tetovaža treba da bude jedinstvena kao i osoba koja je nosi, zbog toga radimo isključivo po porudžbini.
items.en: Random Tattoo Studio is a small, artist-run studio in the heart of Belgrade. We believe every tattoo should be as unique as the person wearing it, which is why we only work custom.

items.label: Bez gotovih dizajna sa zida. Bez kopija. S…
items.sr: Bez gotovih dizajna sa zida. Bez kopija. Samo originalna umetnost napravljena za tebe, od strane umetnika kojima je stalo do svog zanata.
items.en: No flash off the wall. No copies. Just original art made for you, by artists who care about their craft.

items.label: Studio se nalazi na Zvezdari, radi od 2018…
items.sr: Studio se nalazi na Zvezdari, radi od 2018. godine, i prima i zakazane i walk-in klijente.
items.en: The studio is in Zvezdara, Belgrade, has been running since 2018, and takes both booked and walk-in clients.

items.label: Recenzije, uvodni tekst
items.sr: Bez ulepšavanja, ovo su njihove reči. Ljudi koji su nam verovali svoju ideju i izašli sa radom koji nose zauvek.
items.en: No polishing, these are their words. People who trusted us with their idea and walked out with a piece they wear forever.

items.label: Lemson radi u dva sveta koja mali broj ume…
items.sr: Lemson radi u dva sveta koja mali broj umetnika može da premosti, hiperprecizna preciznost crno-belog realizma i slobodna, izražajna energija apstraktnih boja. Bez obzira na stil, svaki komad nosi isti kvalitet: izgleda živo.
items.en: Lemson works across two worlds few artists can bridge, the razor precision of black and grey realism and the loose, expressive energy of abstract colour. Whatever the style, every piece carries the same quality: it looks alive.

items.label: Anjin rad je tih i precizan, i upravo zbog…
items.sr: Anjin rad je tih i precizan, i upravo zbog toga je toliko moćan. Njene tetovaže fine linije su elegantne, promišljene i napravljene da lepo stare. Savršeno za one koji žele nešto rafinirano i duboko lično.
items.en: Anja's work is quiet and precise, and that is exactly why it hits so hard. Her fine line tattoos are elegant, considered and built to age well. Perfect for anyone who wants something refined and deeply personal.

items.label: Enco prenosi ulične zidove na tvoju kožu. …
items.sr: Enco prenosi ulične zidove na tvoju kožu. Ukorenjen u grafiti kulturu, njegov rad je smeo, izražajan i pun karaktera. Ako želiš nešto što privlači pažnju, Enco je tvoj umetnik.
items.en: Enco brings the street walls onto your skin. Rooted in graffiti culture, his work is bold, expressive and full of character. If you want something that turns heads, Enco is your artist.

items.label: Zakaži konsultaciju ili nam napiši poruku.…
items.sr: Zakaži konsultaciju ili nam napiši poruku. Ne moraš da imaš gotovu ideju, dovoljno je da znaš otprilike šta te vuče. Zajedno ćemo iskristalisati.
items.en: Book a consultation or just message us. You do not need a finished idea, knowing roughly what pulls you is enough. We will shape it together.

items.label: Zakaži konsultaciju ili pošalji ideju i re…
items.sr: Zakaži konsultaciju ili pošalji ideju i reference
items.en: Book a consultation or send your idea and references

items.label: Kažemo ti ko od nas je pravi za taj rad
items.sr: Kažemo ti ko od nas je pravi za taj rad
items.en: We tell you which of us is right for the piece

items.label: Dogovorimo veličinu i cenu
items.en: We agree on size and price

items.label: Kad se složimo oko dizajna, rezervišemo ti…
items.sr: Kad se složimo oko dizajna, rezervišemo ti datum. Kapara potvrđuje termin i odbija se od konačne cene.
items.en: Once we agree on the design, we hold a date for you. A deposit confirms the slot and comes off the final price.

items.label: Potvrdiš skicu, veličinu i poziciju
items.en: You confirm the sketch, size and placement

items.label: Dobiješ procenu cene, konačna zavisi od fi…
items.sr: Dobiješ procenu cene, konačna zavisi od finalne veličine i pozicije
items.en: You get a price estimate, the final depends on size and placement

items.label: Dođi naspavan i najeden. Ostalo je na nama…
items.sr: Dođi naspavan i najeden. Ostalo je na nama. Radimo koliko treba, ne koliko je zakazano.
items.en: Come rested and fed. The rest is on us. We work as long as it takes, not as long as it was booked.

items.label: Tetoviranje u studiju, sa pauzama koliko t…
items.sr: Tetoviranje u studiju, sa pauzama koliko ti treba
items.en: Tattooing in the studio, with as many breaks as you need

items.label: Prolazimo kroz negu pre nego što izađeš
items.sr: Prolazimo kroz negu pre nego što izađeš
items.en: We go through aftercare before you leave

items.label: Ostajemo dostupni dok ne zaraste
items.en: We stay reachable until it is healed

items.label: Došao sam sa nejasnom idejom, izašao sa ra…
items.sr: Došao sam sa nejasnom idejom, izašao sa radom koji mi svi komentarišu. Nisu žurili ni sekund.
items.en: I came in with a vague idea and left with a piece everyone comments on. They never rushed a second.

items.label: Čisto, profesionalno, i iskreno mi rekli š…
items.sr: Čisto, profesionalno, i iskreno mi rekli šta neće lepo da stoji. Cenim to više nego da su samo uzeli pare.
items.en: Clean, professional, and they honestly told me what would not sit well. I value that more than them just taking the money.

items.label: Prva tetovaža, bio sam nervozan. Objasnili…
items.sr: Prva tetovaža, bio sam nervozan. Objasnili su sve, pauze kad god mi treba. Vratiću se sigurno.
items.en: First tattoo, I was nervous. They explained everything, breaks whenever I needed. I will definitely be back.

items.label: Fine line rad tako čist da izgleda kao da …
items.sr: Fine line rad tako čist da izgleda kao da je odštampan. Tačno ono što sam tražila.
items.en: Fine line work so clean it looks printed. Exactly what I asked for.

items.label: Zavisi od umetnika, veličine i koliko je r…
items.sr: Zavisi od umetnika, veličine i koliko je rad kompleksan. Zato ne pišemo cenovnik, bio bi netačan. Pošalji nam ideju i dobićeš konkretnu procenu, bez obaveze. Ono što možemo da obećamo: nećeš dobiti iznenađenje na kraju.
items.en: It depends on the artist, the size and how complex the piece is. That is why we do not publish a price list, it would be wrong. Send us your idea and you will get a concrete estimate, no obligation. What we can promise: no surprises at the end.

items.label: Da, ali manje nego što misliš. Zavisi od m…
items.sr: Da, ali manje nego što misliš. Zavisi od mesta, rebra i laktovi su najgori, ruke i noge se lako trpe. Pravimo pauze kad god ti treba. Niko nikad nije pobegao sa stolice.
items.en: Yes, but less than you think. It depends on the spot, ribs and elbows are the worst, arms and legs are easy to take. We break whenever you need. Nobody has ever run off the chair.

items.label: Nemam ideju, samo znam otprilike šta hoću.
items.sr: Nemam ideju, samo znam otprilike šta hoću.
items.en: I have no idea, I only roughly know what I want.

items.label: To je češće nego što misliš i potpuno je u…
items.sr: To je češće nego što misliš i potpuno je u redu. Dođi sa onim što imaš, raspoloženje, motiv, sliku koja ti se sviđa. Naš posao je da to pretvorimo u nešto što stoji na tebi.
items.en: That is more common than you think and completely fine. Come with what you have, a mood, a motif, a picture you like. Our job is to turn that into something that sits on you.

items.label: Mogu li da dođem bez zakazivanja?
items.sr: Mogu li da dođem bez zakazivanja?
items.en: Can I walk in without an appointment?

items.label: Možeš. Za manje radove često možemo odmah,…
items.sr: Možeš. Za manje radove često možemo odmah, za veće ćemo se dogovoriti oko termina. Svrati, popij kafu, pitaj šta te zanima, ne moraš ništa da zakažeš tog dana.
items.en: You can. For smaller pieces we can often do it right away, for bigger ones we will arrange a slot. Drop by, have a coffee, ask what you want, you do not have to book anything that day.

items.label: Zavisi od umetnika i od toga koliko je vel…
items.sr: Zavisi od umetnika i od toga koliko je veliki rad. Javi se pa ćemo ti reći iskreno, ne obećavamo termine koje ne možemo da ispunimo.
items.en: It depends on the artist and how big the piece is. Get in touch and we will tell you honestly, we do not promise slots we cannot keep.

items.label: Šta ako mi se ne dopadne skica?
items.sr: Šta ako mi se ne dopadne skica?
items.en: What if I do not like the sketch?

items.label: Menjamo je. Skica se radi dok ti ne bude p…
items.sr: Menjamo je. Skica se radi dok ti ne bude po volji, nema tetoviranja dok ne kažeš „to je to". Ovo ti ostaje ceo život, nema žurbe.
items.en: We change it. The sketch gets reworked until you are happy, no tattooing until you say "that is it". This stays with you for life, there is no rush.

items.label: Zavisi šta pokrivamo. Pošalji fotografiju …
items.sr: Zavisi šta pokrivamo. Pošalji fotografiju postojeće tetovaže i reći ćemo ti iskreno šta je moguće, a šta nije. Ne prihvatamo cover-up ako mislimo da rezultat neće biti dobar.
items.en: It depends what we are covering. Send a photo of the existing tattoo and we will tell you honestly what is possible and what is not. We do not take on a cover-up if we think the result will not be good.

items.label: Kako se neguje sveža tetovaža?
items.en: How do I care for a fresh tattoo?

items.label: Sve ti objasnimo pre nego što izađeš i dob…
items.sr: Sve ti objasnimo pre nego što izađeš i dobiješ pisano uputstvo. Ukratko: peri, maži, ne češi, izbegavaj sunce, bazen i saunu prve dve nedelje. Ako nešto deluje čudno, javi se, tu smo.
items.en: We explain everything before you leave and you get written instructions. In short: wash it, moisturise it, do not scratch, avoid sun, pools and saunas for the first two weeks. If anything looks off, call us, we are here.

items.label: Paje Jovanovića 33, na Zvezdari u Beogradu…
items.sr: Paje Jovanovića 33, na Zvezdari u Beogradu. Radimo sredom do petka od 12 do 21h, subotom od 12 do 18h. Ponedeljkom i utorkom samo po dogovoru.
items.en: Paje Jovanovića 33, in the Zvezdara area of Belgrade. We work Wednesday to Friday 12 to 21h, Saturday 12 to 18h. Monday and Tuesday by appointment only.

items.label: Koje stilove tetovaža radite?
items.en: What tattoo styles do you do?

items.label: Lemson radi crno-beli realizam, portrete i…
items.sr: Lemson radi crno-beli realizam, portrete i apstraktne radove u boji. Anja radi fine line i linework. Enco radi grafiti i urbani stil. Ako nisi siguran koji stil ti odgovara, dođi na besplatnu konsultaciju.
items.en: Lemson does black and grey realism, portraits and abstract colour work. Anja does fine line and linework. Enco does graffiti and urban style. If you are not sure which style suits you, come in for a free consultation.

items.label: Da li mogu da platim karticom?
items.sr: Da li mogu da platim karticom?

items.label: Da, primamo gotovinu i kartice.
items.en: Yes, we take cash and cards.

items.label: Piši nam ideju ili svrati na kafu. Odgovar…
items.sr: Piši nam ideju ili svrati na kafu. Odgovaramo u roku od 24h.
items.en: Send us your idea or drop by for a coffee. We reply within 24h.

items.label: Svaka dobra tetovaža počinje razgovorom. R…
items.sr: Svaka dobra tetovaža počinje razgovorom. Reci nam šta imaš na umu, stil, ideju, raspoloženje, sliku, i mi ćemo preuzeti od tu. Javićemo ti se da zakažemo besplatnu konsultaciju.
items.en: Every good tattoo starts with a conversation. Tell us what you have in mind, a style, an idea, a mood, a picture, and we will take it from there. We will get back to you to book a free consultation.

items.label: Nisi siguran odakle da počneš? To je sasvi…
items.sr: Nisi siguran odakle da počneš? To je sasvim u redu. Svrati na konsultaciju, besplatna je, bez obaveza, i možda ćeš otići sa idejom na koju nisi ni pomislio.
items.en: Not sure where to start? That is completely fine. Come in for a consultation, it is free, no strings, and you might leave with an idea you never thought of.

titleSr: Zašto svaki tattoo studio insistira na higijeni koliko i na dizajnu
titleEn: Why every tattoo studio insists on hygiene as much as on design
metaTitle: Higijena u Tattoo Studiju | Random Tattoo Beograd
metaDescription: Sterilne igle, rukavice, jednokratni materijal i čist radni prostor razlikuju bezbedan studio od rizičnog. Na šta da obratiš pažnju pre nego što sedneš.
coverAlt: Sterilni pribor u tattoo studiju, Random Tattoo Studio Beograd

children.text: Kada biraš gde ćeš se tetovirati, najčešće gledaš radove majstora, njegov stil i portfolio. To je logično, jer je to ono što ostaje na tvojoj koži zauvek. Ali postoji stvar koja je jednako važna, a koju mnogi početnici potpuno previde, a to je higijena studija. Dobar dizajn u prljavom studiju ne vredi ništa, jer tetovaža nije samo umetnost, već i mali medicinski zahvat.

Svaka tetovaža je, u suštini, otvorena rana. Igla probija kožu na hiljade puta u minuti i time otvara vrata svemu što se nalazi u okolini. Zbog toga ozbiljan studio funkcioniše po pravilima koja liče na ordinaciju. Sve što dolazi u kontakt sa tvojom kožom mora biti ili sterilno i za jednokratnu upotrebu ili propisno dezinfikovano. Igle se koriste jednom i bacaju, nikada se ne dele i nikada se ne koriste ponovo, i to je nešto oko čega nema kompromisa.

Ono što odaje ozbiljan studio jesu detalji koje možeš da primetiš i sam. Majstor pred tobom otvara novu, zapakovanu iglu iz sterilnog pakovanja. Nosi rukavice koje menja kada je potrebno. Radna površina, mašinica i sve što drži u ruci prekriveni su zaštitnom folijom koja se baca posle svake mušterije. Boje se sipaju u male posudice za jednokratnu upotrebu, a ne uzimaju direktno iz zajedničke bočice na način koji bi mogao da je kontaminira. Ako uđeš u studio i vidiš da se ove stvari poštuju, to je dobar znak.

Sterilizacija opreme koja se koristi više puta je posebna priča. Ozbiljni studiji imaju aparat koji se zove autoklav, koji pod visokim pritiskom i temperaturom uništava sve mikroorganizme na priboru. To nije nešto što se radi na oko, već proces koji se prati i beleži. Ako te zanima, potpuno je u redu da pitaš majstora kako sterilišu opremu. Profesionalac se neće uvrediti na to pitanje, naprotiv, biće mu drago što razmišljaš na pravi način.

Higijena se ne završava u studiju, već se nastavlja i kod tebe kod kuće. Majstor ti daje uputstva za negu upravo zato da bi ta otvorena rana zacelila bez problema. Prljave ruke, prljav peškir ili prerano izlaganje bazenu i moru mogu da unesu bakterije i pokvare i najlepši rad, pa čak i da izazovu infekciju. Zbog toga je nega posle tetoviranja jednako deo higijene kao i sve ono što se dešava u studiju.

Poenta je jednostavna. Kada biraš gde ćeš se tetovirati, gledaj radove, ali gledaj i čistoću. Ne ustručavaj se da postaviš pitanja i da obratiš pažnju na to kako studio izgleda i kako se majstor ponaša. Tvoje zdravlje i tvoja koža vrede toga. Najbolji studiji su ponosni na svoju higijenu koliko i na svoje radove, jer znaju da jedno bez drugog ne ide.

When you are choosing where to get tattooed, you usually look at the artist's work, their style and their portfolio. That makes sense, because that is what stays on your skin forever. But there is something equally important that many beginners completely overlook, and that is the studio's hygiene. Good design in a dirty studio is worth nothing, because a tattoo is not only art, it is also a small medical procedure.

Every tattoo is, in essence, an open wound. The needle pierces the skin thousands of times a minute and in doing so opens the door to everything in the surroundings. That is why a serious studio operates by rules that resemble a clinic. Everything that comes into contact with your skin must be either sterile and single use or properly disinfected. Needles are used once and thrown away, never shared and never reused, and there is no compromise on that.

What gives away a serious studio are details you can notice yourself. The artist opens a new, sealed needle from sterile packaging in front of you. They wear gloves and change them when needed. The work surface, the machine and everything they hold are covered with protective film that is thrown away after every client. Inks are poured into small single use caps, not taken directly from a shared bottle in a way that could contaminate it. If you walk into a studio and see these things respected, that is a good sign.

Sterilising equipment that gets reused is a story of its own. Serious studios have a device called an autoclave, which uses high pressure and temperature to destroy every microorganism on the tools. That is not something done by eye, it is a process that is monitored and logged. If you are curious, it is completely fine to ask the artist how they sterilise their equipment. A professional will not be offended by that question; on the contrary, they will be glad you are thinking the right way.

Hygiene does not end in the studio, it continues at your home. The artist gives you aftercare instructions precisely so that open wound heals without trouble. Dirty hands, a dirty towel or getting into a pool or the sea too early can introduce bacteria and ruin even the most beautiful piece, and can even cause an infection. That is why aftercare is just as much a part of hygiene as everything that happens in the studio.

The point is simple. When you are choosing where to get tattooed, look at the work, but look at the cleanliness too. Do not hesitate to ask questions and to pay attention to how the studio looks and how the artist behaves. Your health and your skin are worth it. The best studios are as proud of their hygiene as they are of their work, because they know one does not go without the other.

titleSr: Koža pamti, ali se i menja
titleEn: Skin remembers, but it also changes
metaTitle: Kako Tetovaža Stari | Random Tattoo Beograd
metaDescription: Tetovaža ostaje jer je pigment zaključan u dermisu. Vremenom omekša i blago izbledi, a sunce to ubrzava. Objašnjavamo kako koža čuva mastilo godinama.
coverAlt: Sveža tetovaža tokom zaceljivanja, Random Tattoo Studio Beograd

children.text: Većina ljudi misli da tetovaža jednostavno stoji na koži, kao neka nalepnica koja s vremenom počne da bledi. Istina je mnogo zanimljivija i ima veze sa načinom na koji tvoje telo funkcioniše na nivou koji golim okom ne možeš da vidiš.

Kada te majstor tetovira, igla ne ostavlja mastilo na površini kože. Ona probija gornji sloj, koji se zove epidermis, i ostavlja pigment u dubljem sloju, dermisu. To je ključni razlog zašto tetovaža ostaje ceo život. Epidermis se, naime, obnavlja neprestano. Svakih nekoliko nedelja tvoje telo praktično zameni ceo gornji sloj kože novim ćelijama. Da mastilo stoji tu, tetovaža bi ti nestala za mesec dana, kao da si je nacrtao flomasterom. Ali pošto je pigment zaključan dublje, ostaje na mestu.

Ono što se dešava odmah nakon tetoviranja je prava mala bitka unutar tvog tela. Tvoj imuni sistem prepoznaje čestice mastila kao strano telo i šalje ćelije koje se zovu makrofagi da ih „pojedu” i uklone. Problem je, iz njihove perspektive, u tome što su čestice pigmenta prevelike da bi ih u potpunosti razgradili. Tako makrofagi jednostavno ostaju zaglavljeni sa tim česticama, držeći ih na mestu godinama. Kada takva ćelija umre, druga preuzme pigment. Tvoja tetovaža je zapravo u stanju stalnog, tihog održavanja koje tvoje telo obavlja bez tvog znanja.

Zato tetovaže vremenom omekšaju i blago izblede. Sitne linije koje su na početku bile oštre kao žilet, posle deset ili petnaest godina postanu malo mekše i šire. To nije znak lošeg rada, već prirodan proces. Sunce dodatno ubrzava bledjenje, jer UV zraci razgrađuju pigment, i upravo zato ljudi koji čuvaju tetovaže od sunca i redovno ih mažu kremom imaju radove koji izgledaju sveže i posle mnogo godina.

Zanimljivo je i to da koža na različitim delovima tela drži mastilo drugačije. Mesta gde je koža deblja i gde ima manje trenja, poput nadlaktice ili lista, obično zadrže tetovažu jasnijom duže vreme. Delovi kao što su šake, prsti i stopala su poznati po tome što brzo blede, jer se ta koža najviše koristi, često pere i izložena je stalnom trenju. Zbog toga mnogi majstori unapred upozore mušteriju da će tetovaža na prstu verovatno morati da se dorađuje.

Sve ovo znači jednu lepu stvar. Tvoja tetovaža nije mrtva slika na koži. Ona je deo živog tkiva koje se menja zajedno sa tobom, koje stari kada ti stariš i koje tvoje telo aktivno čuva svakog dana. To je možda i najlepši razlog zašto su tetovaže toliko lične.

Most people think a tattoo just sits on the skin, like a sticker that slowly starts to fade. The truth is far more interesting, and it has everything to do with how your body works at a level you cannot see with the naked eye.

When an artist tattoos you, the needle does not leave ink on the surface of the skin. It pierces the top layer, called the epidermis, and deposits pigment in the deeper layer, the dermis. That is the key reason a tattoo stays for life. The epidermis renews itself constantly. Every few weeks your body essentially replaces the entire top layer of skin with new cells. If the ink sat there, your tattoo would be gone in a month, as if you had drawn it with a marker. But because the pigment is locked in deeper, it stays put.

What happens right after tattooing is a small battle inside your body. Your immune system recognises the ink particles as foreign and sends cells called macrophages to „eat” and remove them. The problem, from their point of view, is that the pigment particles are too big to break down completely. So the macrophages simply end up stuck holding those particles, keeping them in place for years. When one of those cells dies, another takes over the pigment. Your tattoo is actually in a state of constant, quiet maintenance your body performs without you knowing.

That is why tattoos soften and fade slightly over time. Fine lines that were razor sharp at the start become a little softer and wider after ten or fifteen years. That is not a sign of bad work, it is a natural process. The sun speeds up the fading, because UV rays break down pigment, and that is exactly why people who keep their tattoos out of the sun and moisturise them regularly have pieces that still look fresh many years later.

It is also interesting that skin on different parts of the body holds ink differently. Places where the skin is thicker and there is less friction, like the upper arm or the calf, usually keep a tattoo sharper for longer. Areas such as hands, fingers and feet are known for fading fast, because that skin is used the most, washed often and exposed to constant friction. That is why many artists warn a client up front that a finger tattoo will probably need touching up.

All of this means one beautiful thing. Your tattoo is not a dead picture on your skin. It is part of living tissue that changes along with you, that ages when you age, and that your body actively protects every single day. That is perhaps the loveliest reason why tattoos are so personal.

titleSr: Zašto ne smeš da veruješ svemu što pročitaš o tetovažama
titleEn: Why you should not believe everything you read about tattoos
metaTitle: Mitovi o Tetovažama | Random Tattoo Beograd
metaDescription: Razdvajamo najčešće mitove o tetovažama od činjenica: bledenje, bol, cene, sunce i nega. Šta je istina, a šta zabluda koja se prenosi godinama.
coverAlt: Detalj tetovaže na koži, Random Tattoo Studio Beograd

children.text: Malo koja tema ima toliko mitova oko sebe kao tetoviranje. Priče se prenose sa kolena na koleno, sa foruma na forum, i vremenom se toliko ukorene da ljudi u njih veruju kao u činjenice. Vredi razbiti neke od najčešćih, jer pogrešna verovanja često plaše ljude bez razloga ili ih navode na loše odluke.

Jedan od najpoznatijih mitova kaže da ne smeš da se tetoviraš ako imaš mladež ili puno pega. Istina je da dobar majstor jednostavno neće tetovirati preko mladeža, i to ne zato što je opasno za tetovažu, već zato što je važno da mladež ostane vidljiv radi praćenja zdravlja kože. Umesto da preskoči čitav deo tela, majstor će jednostavno ostaviti mali razmak oko njega i dizajn se prilagodi tako da to niko i ne primeti.

Druga rasprostranjena zabluda je da tetovaže „kvare” znojenje ili da osoba sa velikim tetovažama ne može normalno da se znoji. To jednostavno nije tačno. Mastilo se nalazi u dermisu, a znojne žlezde funkcionišu potpuno nezavisno od pigmenta. Ljudi sa telom prekrivenim tetovažama znoje se isto kao i svi ostali. Ovaj mit verovatno potiče od toga što sveža tetovaža, dok zaceljuje, privremeno menja način na koji koža reaguje, ali to prođe za par nedelja.

Postoji i verovanje da su tanke, sitne linije „lakše” za telo i da manje bole nego velike tetovaže. Ironično, često je obrnuto. Vrlo fine linije zahtevaju precizne i spore prolaze iglom, dok popunjavanje velikih površina ide brže i telo ga ponekad podnese lakše. Veličina tetovaže ne govori direktno o tome koliko će boleti, mnogo je važnije mesto na telu i tehnika koja se koristi.

Čest je i mit da tetovaža mora da bude skupa da bi bila dobra, ili obrnuto, da je jeftina tetovaža isto što i loša. Cena zavisi od mnogo faktora, iskustva majstora, veličine i detalja, ali prava mera kvaliteta je portfolio majstora i higijena studija, a ne sam iznos. Najpametnije je da gledaš radove, a ne cenu, jer tetovažu nosiš ceo život.

Na kraju, tu je i priča da tetovaže ne mogu da se uklone ili poprave. Iako je uklanjanje laserom proces koji traje i nije jeftin, danas je sasvim moguće. Isto tako, veliki broj naizgled „propalih” tetovaža može da se pretvori u nešto lepo kroz takozvani cover up, gde vešt majstor iskoristi stari rad kao osnovu za novi dizajn. Malo koja greška je zaista trajna presuda.

Few subjects carry as many myths as tattooing. Stories get passed down from person to person, from forum to forum, and over time they take root so deeply that people believe them as fact. It is worth breaking down some of the most common ones, because wrong beliefs often scare people off for no reason or push them into bad decisions.

One of the best known myths says you cannot get tattooed if you have moles or lots of freckles. The truth is that a good artist simply will not tattoo over a mole, and not because it is dangerous for the tattoo, but because it matters that the mole stays visible so your skin health can be monitored. Instead of skipping an entire part of the body, the artist will just leave a small gap around it and the design adapts so that nobody even notices.

Another widespread misconception is that tattoos „ruin” sweating, or that a person with large tattoos cannot sweat normally. That is simply not true. The ink sits in the dermis, and sweat glands work completely independently of pigment. People covered in tattoos sweat exactly like everyone else. This myth probably comes from the fact that a fresh tattoo, while it heals, temporarily changes how the skin behaves, but that passes within a couple of weeks.

There is also a belief that thin, small lines are „easier” on the body and hurt less than large tattoos. Ironically, it is often the opposite. Very fine lines demand precise, slow passes with the needle, while filling large areas goes faster and the body sometimes takes it more easily. The size of a tattoo does not directly tell you how much it will hurt; the spot on the body and the technique used matter far more.

Another common myth is that a tattoo has to be expensive to be good, or the reverse, that a cheap tattoo is the same as a bad one. Price depends on many factors, the artist's experience, the size and the detail, but the real measure of quality is the artist's portfolio and the studio's hygiene, not the amount itself. The smartest thing is to look at the work, not the price, because you wear the tattoo for life.

Finally, there is the story that tattoos cannot be removed or fixed. Although laser removal is a process that takes time and is not cheap, today it is entirely possible. In the same way, a large number of seemingly „ruined” tattoos can be turned into something beautiful through a so-called cover up, where a skilled artist uses the old piece as the base for a new design. Very few mistakes are truly a life sentence.

titleSr: Osećaj bola zavisi od mesta na telu
titleEn: How much it hurts depends on where you put it
metaTitle: Da Li Boli Tetovaža | Random Tattoo Beograd
metaDescription: Bol zavisi od mesta na telu. Rebra i prsti su najzahtevniji, nadlaktica i butina najlakši. Objašnjavamo od čega zavisi osećaj i kako se pripremiti.
coverAlt: Tetoviranje nadlaktice u studiju, Random Tattoo Studio Beograd

children.text: Prvo pitanje koje skoro svako postavi pre svoje prve tetovaže glasi: koliko boli? Iskren odgovor je da ne postoji jedan odgovor, jer bol nije isti na svakom delu tela. Neko mesto ćeš jedva osetiti, a drugo će te naterati da stisneš zube. Da bi znao šta te čeka, dobro je da razumeš od čega taj osećaj zapravo zavisi.

Glavna stvar koja određuje koliko će boleti jeste koliko je koža na tom mestu blizu kosti i koliko ima mekog tkiva ispod nje. Tamo gde je koža tanka i odmah ispod nje se nalazi kost, osećaj je oštriji i intenzivniji. Zato su mesta kao što su rebra, gležnjevi, prsti, ključna kost i lakat poznata kao zahtevnija. Igla praktično vibrira uz kost i to tvoje telo veoma jasno oseti.

Sa druge strane, delovi tela gde ima više mišića i masnog tkiva podnose se mnogo lakše. Nadlaktica, spoljna strana ruke, list i butina imaju taj mekani sloj koji ublažava osećaj. Mnogi ljudi koji su tetovirali i rebra i nadlakticu kažu da su te dve stvari kao dan i noć. Zbog toga se prva tetovaža često preporučuje baš na nekom od tih mekših mesta, da bi čovek prošao kroz iskustvo bez preteranog stresa.

Postoji i deo priče koji nema veze sa mestom, već sa tvojim telom u tom trenutku. Kada počne tetoviranje, telo oslobađa adrenalin, i zato mnogi kažu da je prvih desetak minuta najintenzivnije. Posle toga telo se prilagodi, adrenalin i endorfini urade svoje, i osećaj postane podnošljiviji. Zbog toga duže seanse imaju svoj ritam, gde su početak i sam kraj, kada je telo umorno, obično najteži delovi.

Ono što mnogi ne znaju jeste koliko tvoje opšte stanje utiče na doživljaj bola. Ako dođeš na tetoviranje neispavan, gladan ili mamuran, sve će te boleti mnogo više. Nizak nivo šećera u krvi čini telo osetljivijim, pa je pravilo svakog dobrog majstora da mušterija pre dolaska nešto pojede i da se dobro naspava. Voda je takođe važna, jer hidrirana koža lakše prima mastilo i lakše se tetovira.

Vredi znati i da svako telo doživljava bol drugačije. Ono što je jednoj osobi nepodnošljivo, drugoj je sasvim u redu, i to nema veze sa hrabrošću, već sa načinom na koji nervni sistem svakog čoveka reaguje. Zato nema smisla porediti se sa drugima. Najbolji savet je da dišeš mirno, da ne zadržavaš dah i da se ne grčiš, jer napet mišić boli više nego opušten. Ako ti u nekom trenutku bude previše, svaki majstor koji drži do sebe će rado napraviti kratku pauzu.

The first question almost everyone asks before their first tattoo is: how much does it hurt? The honest answer is that there is no single answer, because the pain is not the same everywhere on the body. Some spots you will barely feel, others will have you gritting your teeth. To know what is coming, it helps to understand what that feeling actually depends on.

The main thing that determines how much it will hurt is how close the skin is to bone at that spot, and how much soft tissue sits underneath. Where the skin is thin and bone is right beneath it, the sensation is sharper and more intense. That is why places like ribs, ankles, fingers, collarbone and elbow are known as the demanding ones. The needle practically vibrates against the bone and your body feels that very clearly.

On the other hand, parts of the body with more muscle and fat are much easier to take. The upper arm, the outside of the arm, the calf and the thigh have that soft layer that cushions the feeling. Many people who have tattooed both ribs and upper arm say the two are night and day. That is why a first tattoo is often recommended on one of those softer spots, so you can go through the experience without too much stress.

There is also a part of the story that has nothing to do with location and everything to do with your body in that moment. When tattooing starts, the body releases adrenaline, which is why many say the first ten minutes are the most intense. After that the body adapts, adrenaline and endorphins do their work, and the feeling becomes more bearable. That is why longer sessions have their own rhythm, where the beginning and the very end, when the body is tired, are usually the hardest parts.

What many people do not know is how much your general state affects the pain. If you show up sleep deprived, hungry or hungover, everything will hurt far more. Low blood sugar makes the body more sensitive, which is why every good artist has a rule that the client eats something beforehand and gets a proper night of sleep. Water matters too, because hydrated skin takes ink more easily and is easier to tattoo.

It is also worth knowing that every body experiences pain differently. What is unbearable to one person is perfectly fine for another, and that has nothing to do with toughness, only with how each person's nervous system reacts. So there is no point comparing yourself to others. The best advice is to breathe calmly, not hold your breath and not tense up, because a tense muscle hurts more than a relaxed one. And if it ever gets to be too much, any artist worth their salt will gladly take a short break.

titleSr: Šta se zapravo dešava dok tvoja tetovaža zaceljuje
titleEn: What actually happens while your tattoo heals
metaTitle: Zaceljivanje Tetovaže Dan Po Dan | Random Tattoo
metaDescription: Zaceljivanje tetovaže ide u fazama tokom nekoliko nedelja. Šta se dešava dan po dan, od svežeg rada do zarasle kože, i kako da negu odradiš kako treba.
coverAlt: Sveža tetovaža u prvoj fazi zaceljivanja, Random Tattoo Studio Beograd

children.text: Trenutak kada izađeš iz studija sa svežom tetovažom je tek početak priče. Ono što se dešava tokom sledećih nekoliko nedelja odlučuje da li će tvoja tetovaža izgledati oštro i živo ili mutno i izbledelo. Razumevanje tog procesa pomaže ti da ne paničiš kada primetiš stvari koje su potpuno normalne, i da prepoznaš kada nešto zaista nije u redu.

Prvih nekoliko dana tvoja koža se ponaša kao da je posekotina, jer to u suštini i jeste. Sveža tetovaža je otvorena rana i tvoje telo odmah reaguje. Normalno je da to mesto bude crveno, blago otečeno i toplo na dodir. Iz tetovaže se prvog dana često izlučuje mešavina viška mastila, plazme i limfe, i to je potpuno prirodno. Upravo zato majstori savetuju da se prvog dana tetovaža nežno opere i da se ne pokriva predugo, kako bi mogla da diše.

Otprilike od trećeg do šestog dana počinje faza koja mnoge iznenadi i uplaši, a to je ljuštenje. Koža počne da se suši i da se ljušti u sitnim ljuspicama, baš kao kada preplaneš na suncu. U tim ljuspicama često se vidi boja tvoje tetovaže, pa ljudi pomisle da im mastilo otpada i da će tetovaža nestati. Nema razloga za paniku. To je samo mrtvi gornji sloj kože koji otpada, dok pravo mastilo ostaje bezbedno u dubljem sloju. U ovoj fazi je najvažnije da odoliš iskušenju da čačkaš ili čupaš te ljuspice, jer time možeš da izvučeš pigment pre vremena i napraviš rupe u tetovaži.

Negde oko druge nedelje tetovaža uđe u fazu koju mnogi opišu kao čudan osećaj. Ljuštenje je uglavnom gotovo, ali koža preko tetovaže može da izgleda pomalo mutno, kao da je prekrivena tankim slojem. Ta zamućenost je sasvim normalna i nastaje jer se ispod površine formira nova, sveža koža koja još nije potpuno prozirna. Tokom sledećih nedelja ta magla se povuče i tetovaža ponovo dobije svoju punu jasnoću i sjaj. Zbog toga nikada ne treba suditi o konačnom izgledu tetovaže dok potpuno ne zaceli.

Iako je površinsko zaceljivanje uglavnom gotovo za dve do tri nedelje, duboko zaceljivanje traje mnogo duže, često i do nekoliko meseci. U tom periodu koža ispod površine i dalje radi na tome da se u potpunosti oporavi. Zato je pametno da još neko vreme nakon što tetovaža deluje zaceljeno nastaviš da je hidriraš i čuvaš od jakog sunca. Nega u ovom periodu direktno utiče na to koliko će rad izgledati lepo na duže staze.

Kroz sve ovo, ključna reč je strpljenje. Najčešće greške ne prave majstori, već mušterije koje ne poštuju proces zaceljivanja, čačkaju ranu, previše je kvase ili je izlažu suncu i bazenu prerano. Ako svom telu daš vremena i pratiš uputstva majstora, nagradiće te tetovažom koja izgleda tačno onako kako si zamislio. Tvoja tetovaža je zajednički rad, majstor uradi svoj deo u studiju, a ti završiš posao kod kuće tokom narednih nedelja.

The moment you walk out of the studio with a fresh tattoo is only the beginning of the story. What happens over the next few weeks decides whether your tattoo will look sharp and alive or dull and faded. Understanding that process helps you not panic when you notice things that are completely normal, and to recognise when something genuinely is wrong.

For the first few days your skin behaves as if it has a cut, because that is essentially what it is. A fresh tattoo is an open wound and your body reacts immediately. It is normal for the area to be red, slightly swollen and warm to the touch. On the first day the tattoo often weeps a mix of excess ink, plasma and lymph, and that is completely natural. That is exactly why artists advise washing the tattoo gently on day one and not covering it for too long, so it can breathe.

Roughly from the third to the sixth day comes the phase that surprises and scares many people, and that is peeling. The skin starts to dry and flake off in small pieces, just like when you have been sunburnt. The colour of your tattoo is often visible in those flakes, so people think the ink is falling out and the tattoo will disappear. There is no reason to panic. That is only the dead top layer of skin coming off, while the real ink stays safely in the deeper layer. In this phase the most important thing is to resist the urge to pick or pull at those flakes, because that can pull pigment out early and leave holes in your tattoo.

Around the second week the tattoo enters a phase many describe as a strange feeling. The peeling is mostly done, but the skin over the tattoo can look slightly cloudy, as if covered by a thin film. That cloudiness is perfectly normal and happens because new, fresh skin is forming below the surface and is not fully transparent yet. Over the following weeks that haze lifts and the tattoo regains its full clarity and shine. That is why you should never judge the final look of a tattoo before it is completely healed.

Although surface healing is mostly done within two to three weeks, deep healing takes much longer, often up to a few months. During that period the skin below the surface is still working on fully recovering. That is why it is smart to keep moisturising it and keeping it out of strong sun for a while even after the tattoo looks healed. Care in this period directly affects how good the piece looks in the long run.

Through all of this, the key word is patience. The most common mistakes are not made by artists, but by clients who do not respect the healing process, pick at the wound, soak it too much or expose it to sun and pools too early. If you give your body time and follow your artist's instructions, it will reward you with a tattoo that looks exactly the way you imagined. Your tattoo is a joint effort: the artist does their part in the studio, and you finish the job at home over the following weeks.

titleEn: How your lifestyle shapes your tattoo years later

children.text: Kada ljudi biraju tetovažu, obično razmišljaju samo o tome kako će izgledati onog dana kada izađu iz studija. Retko ko se zapita kako će taj isti rad izgledati za pet, deset ili dvadeset godina. A istina je da tvoja tetovaža ne živi u vakuumu, ona stari zajedno sa tobom i sve što radiš sa svojim telom ostavlja trag na njoj.

Najveći neprijatelj svake tetovaže je sunce. UV zraci polako razgrađuju čestice pigmenta u koži i vremenom čine boje bleđim i mutnijim. Osoba koja provodi mnogo vremena na suncu bez zaštite imaće tetovaže koje mnogo brže gube na oštrini, dok neko ko redovno maže kremu za sunčanje preko svojih radova može da ih sačuva svežim decenijama. Zbog toga iskusni majstori uvek kažu da je krema sa visokim faktorom najbolji prijatelj svake tetovaže.

Promene telesne težine su druga velika stvar koju ljudi ne uzimaju u obzir. Koža je elastična, ali ima svoje granice. Naglo dobijanje ili gubljenje kilograma može da razvuče ili blago izobliči tetovažu, posebno ako se nalazi na mestima poput stomaka, ruku ili butina, gde se koža najviše menja. Kod žena je čest primer trudnoća, kada tetovaže na stomaku ili bokovima mogu da promene oblik. To ne znači da treba izbegavati te delove, već da je dobro znati kako telo funkcioniše i eventualno birati stabilnija mesta ako planiraš veće promene.

Zanimanje i svakodnevne navike takođe igraju ulogu. Ljudi koji rade fizičke poslove, često peru ruke ili rade sa hemikalijama primetiće da tetovaže na šakama i podlakticama brže blede od onih na skrivenijim delovima tela. Isto važi i za sportiste čija koža trpi mnogo trenja. Tetovaža na mestu koje je stalno u pokretu i pod pritiskom jednostavno će zahtevati više pažnje i povremene dorade.

Ni ishrana i hidratacija nisu nevažne. Koža koja je dobro hidrirana i negovana bolje zadržava pigment i izgleda zdravije, pa samim tim i tetovaža na njoj izgleda lepše. Pušenje, s druge strane, utiče na kvalitet i elastičnost kože tokom godina, što se posredno odražava i na to kako stare tvoji radovi. Ništa od ovoga ne znači da moraš da promeniš ceo život zbog jedne tetovaže, ali vredi razumeti da je nega kože zapravo nega tetovaže.

Poenta svega je jednostavna. Tetovaža nije nešto što uradiš i zaboraviš. Ona je deo tebe koji zahteva malo pažnje da bi lepo ostario. Oni koji to razumeju i posvete par minuta nedeljno nezi svojih radova, uživaju u tetovažama koje i posle mnogo godina izgledaju gotovo kao onog prvog dana.

When people choose a tattoo, they usually only think about how it will look on the day they walk out of the studio. Rarely does anyone ask how that same piece will look in five, ten or twenty years. And the truth is that your tattoo does not live in a vacuum, it ages along with you and everything you do with your body leaves a mark on it.

The greatest enemy of every tattoo is the sun. UV rays slowly break down pigment particles in the skin and over time make the colours paler and murkier. Someone who spends a lot of time in the sun without protection will have tattoos that lose their sharpness far faster, while someone who regularly applies sunscreen over their pieces can keep them fresh for decades. That is why experienced artists always say that a high factor sunscreen is every tattoo's best friend.

Changes in body weight are the second big thing people do not take into account. Skin is elastic, but it has its limits. Rapid weight gain or loss can stretch or slightly distort a tattoo, especially if it sits on places like the stomach, arms or thighs, where the skin changes the most. With women a common example is pregnancy, when tattoos on the stomach or hips can change shape. That does not mean you should avoid those areas, only that it is good to know how the body works and perhaps choose more stable spots if you are planning big changes.

Your job and everyday habits also play a role. People who do physical work, wash their hands often or handle chemicals will notice that tattoos on the hands and forearms fade faster than those on more hidden parts of the body. The same goes for athletes whose skin takes a lot of friction. A tattoo in a spot that is constantly moving and under pressure will simply demand more attention and the occasional touch up.

Diet and hydration are not irrelevant either. Skin that is well hydrated and cared for holds pigment better and looks healthier, and so a tattoo on it looks better too. Smoking, on the other hand, affects the quality and elasticity of the skin over the years, which indirectly shows in how your pieces age. None of this means you have to change your whole life for one tattoo, but it is worth understanding that caring for your skin is caring for your tattoo.

The point of it all is simple. A tattoo is not something you get and forget. It is a part of you that needs a little attention to age well. Those who understand that and give a couple of minutes a week to caring for their pieces enjoy tattoos that still look almost like day one many years later.
